column2: req_desc

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from /app/run.json and answers the health check as specified in Deployment.

Seeded sign-in and roles
Every seeded person signs in with their email and the shared seed password and reaches only the screens and endpoints their role allows, as qualified in API.

One error shape and order
Every API error uses the one error shape and the one precedence order stated in API, with validation reporting every invalid field at once.

Server boundary
The server rejects cross-origin writes, oversized and non-JSON bodies, and never serves source files or credentials, as qualified in Server boundary.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment variables in Configuration and secrets and never appears in source or in anything sent to the browser.

Three viewports without overflow
Every screen lays out as described in Screens and layout at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no horizontal scrolling.

Warm clinical look
Pages use the warm off-white ground, hairline-ruled data rows, the serif and sans pairing, right-aligned tabular figures and terracotta only on the seal, as described in Visual design.

Calm motion
Nothing on any screen moves except the motions listed in Motion and effects, and none of them loops.

Keyboard focus
Every control is reachable with Tab in visual order and shows a visible focus ring, and every dialog traps focus, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener.

Reduced motion
With reduced motion requested, each motion is replaced by the substitute stated in Motion and effects.

Contrast and tap targets
All text meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast on its background and every control is at least 44 by 44 pixels at 375x812.

Buy a self-paced course
A learner nurse opens a published self-paced course, pays their share in the Checkout dialog, and lands back on the course with a receipt in their inbox.

Employer and learner shares
Checkout splits the list price between the nurse's hospital and the nurse under the coverage policy in effect at the checkout instant, so the two shares add up to the list price to the cent, by the rule in Business rules.

Checkout retries charge once
Repeating a checkout with the same idempotency key and body returns the original success without a second charge, reusing the key with a different body is rejected, and a failed checkout leaves its key unused, as stated in Business rules.

Payment, enrolment and receipt together
A checkout either records its Kill Bill payments, confirms the enrolment and sends one receipt, or leaves no enrolment, no payment and no email, including while Kill Bill is down.

Keyboard checkout
A learner nurse can open the Checkout dialog, choose a cohort, pay and dismiss the dialog using only the keyboard.

Enrol in a live cohort
A learner nurse picks an open cohort of a cohort course, pays, and sees that cohort's seats remaining drop by one.

Last cohort seat
When several learner nurses check out the last seat of a capped cohort at the same moment, exactly one is enrolled and every other one is told the cohort is full and offered the waitlist.

Cohort waitlist
A learner nurse can join and leave the waitlist of a full cohort and sees their position, and learners who join at the same moment get distinct positions, as qualified in Business rules.

Cohort enrolment closes
Checkout and waitlist joins on a cohort are refused from the cohort's close instant onward, as stated in Business rules.

Run a capped cohort
The nurse planner creates a cohort with a seat cap and close date, changes its cap, and follows its roster, seats remaining and waitlist.

Seats remaining recomputed
A cohort's seats remaining always equals its seat cap minus its active enrolments, after enrolments, refunds and seat-cap changes.

Cohort rosters stay with the provider
Only the nurse planner sees a cohort's roster and waitlist names, and any other user reading a cohort gets only its public summary.

Buy a seat pack
A sponsor coordinator buys a pack of seats for a published self-paced course and sees it in their pack list with its balance and expiry date.

Pack purchase charged once
A pack purchase records one Kill Bill payment on the hospital's account, a replay with the same idempotency key makes no second charge, and no pack is created while Kill Bill is down.

Paired seat ledger
Every seat movement in a pack is two ledger entries that cancel out, and the pack balance always equals the sum of its pack entries and never drops below zero.

Assign a seat to a nurse
A sponsor coordinator assigns a seat from a pack to one of their hospital's nurses, who gets an invitation email and a confirmed enrolment.

Last seat in a pack
When two assignments race for a pack's last seat, exactly one succeeds and the other is told the pack is empty.

Return an unused seat
A sponsor coordinator can return a seat whose nurse has not verified any module, which withdraws that enrolment and puts the seat back in the pack.

Unassigned seats expire
Seats still unassigned when a pack expires leave the pack through exactly one expiry movement, even when several requests first touch the pack at once, and cannot be assigned afterwards, as timed in Business rules.

Study the modules
A learner nurse works through each lesson, answers its knowledge check, and sees each verified module's glyph and their progress update.

Module verification
A lesson becomes verified only when its knowledge-check answer is correct, and the post-evaluation opens only after every lesson is verified.

Learner records stay private
A learner nurse can read only their own enrolments, modules, certificates, transcript and PDFs, and any other id answers as not found.

Keyboard module player
A learner nurse can move between modules, answer each knowledge check and submit the post-evaluation using only the keyboard.

Finish a course and get a certificate
Submitting the post-evaluation takes a learner nurse to the completion screen, where the Seal press shows their sealed certificate with its hours and serial.

Awarded contact hours
A certificate's contact hours are the course's verified learning minutes divided by 60, rounded down to the nearest quarter hour and fixed at issue.

One certificate per course run
Double-submitting the post-evaluation or refreshing the completion screen always yields the same single certificate and serial.

Certificate, PDF and email together
A certificate counts as sealed only after its PDF is stored, its email goes out exactly once after that, and while storage is down it waits in the pending state described in Services.

Seal press
On the completion screen the verified module chips fly into proportional wedges of the seal, the numeral counts up to the awarded hours and the ring text appears, as specified in Motion and effects.

Pending seal
While the certificate PDF is pending, the seal stays open at the top with its pending label, the Share with a verifier button stays disabled, and the screen updates as stated in Feedback states.

Seal craft
The seal reads as a pressed terracotta mark whose wedges, hatched unverified segments, centre numeral and ring text are legible and balanced at every viewport.

Share a certificate with a verifier
A learner nurse creates a verification link from their transcript, a verifier opens it without signing in, and the nurse can revoke it.

Verification links
Verification links are unguessable, limited to one active link per certificate, stop working when revoked or replaced, and expire, as qualified in Business rules.

Public verification page
A verification link shows that one certificate's summary and PDF and nothing else, and every attempt to change anything through it is refused.

Private fields stay private
Certificate emails, certificate PDFs and verification pages never contain the nurse's licence number, date of birth, email address, or any price or payment split.

Request and approve a refund
A learner nurse requests a refund for a paid enrolment, and the nurse planner approves or declines it from the refund queue, whose row then names who decided it and when.

Refund amount
An approved refund is full, prorated by unfinished minutes, or refused, according to the refund rule in Business rules.

Refund split
An approved refund is split between the hospital and the nurse in the ratio of their original shares, adds up to the refund total to the cent, and is recorded as Kill Bill refunds keyed to the request so a retried approval never refunds twice, while Credwell changes nothing when Kill Bill is down.

Reissue or revoke a certificate
The nurse planner reissues a certificate after a name correction or revokes it, and the nurse's transcript and verification link reflect the change once the reissue is sealed or the revoke is recorded.

Reissue keeps the serial
A reissue keeps the certificate's serial and hours, stores a new PDF version while keeping the old one, emails the nurse once, and of concurrent reissue or revoke requests on one certificate exactly one is accepted when the first accepted is a revoke or a still-sealing reissue, as qualified in Business rules.

Transcript totals recomputed
A learner nurse's total earned hours always equals the sum of their sealed certificates, counting each certificate once, including while a reissue is pending and after a rename.

Review hospital compliance
A sponsor coordinator reviews their totals, searches their nurses, reads the monthly hours report and downloads a completions CSV.

Hospital-only totals and search
Dashboard totals, nurse search, the monthly report and exports include only the coordinator's own hospital's nurses and seats, grouped and filtered by each certificate's provider-time issue date.

Safe completions export
The completions CSV is stored under the hospital's folder in object storage and neutralises every cell that a spreadsheet would read as a formula.

Coordinator record access
A sponsor coordinator can open certificates and nurse records only for enrolments their hospital funded, and any other id answers as not found.

Draft, review and publish a course
A course author drafts a course and submits it, and the nurse planner returns it with a note or publishes it, then later withdraws it.

Course lifecycle
Courses move only along the legal edges in Business rules, each edge only by its permitted role, every accepted move raises the version by one, and withdrawn courses keep their certificates valid.

Stale course edits
Saving or moving a course with a version someone else has already changed is rejected with the current version number, and nothing changes.

Effective-dated coverage
A sponsor coordinator sets a tuition-coverage percentage effective today or from a later date, and a checkout whose quoted learner share no longer matches the policy in effect is refused with the new quote and nothing charged.

Close instant in provider time
Every cohort publishes its close instant as 23:59:59.999 on its close date in the provider's time zone, correct across daylight-saving changes, and shows it in Central Time.

Unaccepted fields refused
A request body carrying a field its endpoint does not name answers 422 naming each such field and changes nothing, as qualified in API.

Exact link expiry
Verification links and emailed download links stop working at exactly their server-side expiry instant, an expired verification link is listed as expired rather than revoked, and every capability response is served uncached and without a referrer.

Attributed refund decisions
Each refund decision is written once with the deciding planner, time and note and never changes, and every Kill Bill write names the acting Credwell user, as stated in Services.

Copies carry the version's name
Every certificate copy carries the nurse name of the certificate's current version rather than the live display name, and the version history keeps every earlier name.

Bounded literal search
Nurse and certificate searches match text literally and accept at most 100 characters, and a completions export spans at most 366 days, as stated in API.
/app/run.json exists and holds exactly the string keys _schema (value run-manifest-v1), install, build and serve.
/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md names every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and every bundled font, with its licence.

Every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) uses MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0 or CC0-1.0, and bundled fonts use OFL-1.1.
The app stores data only in the provided Postgres, Kill Bill, MinIO and Mailpit services, with no SQLite, Redis, in-process persistent store or local files as a record store.
The provided service definitions and their credential values stay unchanged.
All application source is TypeScript; plain JavaScript appears only in tool configuration files.
The running app makes no browser requests to third-party origins (no font, script or analytics CDNs).
